title: Free deal discovery feeds
purpose: Automatically collect published deal mentions across retailers without requiring a developer key. Feed mentions are leads, not confirmed stock, completed sales or profitable purchases.
steps: Open Discover. Recent mentions appear in the discovery inbox after a permitted feed request succeeds. No API key is needed.
Open Settings to see each feed’s last success or access error. Each feed runs at most once per 15 minutes and respects robots policy, server rate limits and Pause.
Supported canonical merchant links are queued automatically for product enrichment. Other published mentions stay in the discovery inbox; they are not priced products.
The item then opens in Product research. Compare exact identity, resale evidence, destination costs and regional availability before considering a purchase.
A community post may be old, unavailable, region-specific, conditional or mistaken. Re-fetching the feed does not reset its published or first-seen age.
cost: No paid feed API, subscription or proxy is configured. Public source access and permitted use must hold.
limitation: Actual access is reported per source in Settings. A feed mention is not product inventory. A redirect, robots denial or malformed document is reported without sample replacements.

title: Included retailer observations
purpose: Automatically import published product prices, photos and stock declarations from supported US retailer catalogs.
steps: Opening the app automatically starts collection unless you paused it. No product URL or price entry is required for the included catalogs.

The startup queue prioritizes the US Arduino catalog and eight Adafruit category catalogs, including clearance, tools and sensors. Prices, photos and stock declarations appear after each source finishes.
Incomplete catalog backfills continue on a shorter bounded schedule. Completed category catalogs refresh every 15 minutes; access and response-size failures stay visible in Settings.
Sources browses collected products grouped by retailer. Configure optional production eBay access here for supported active-listing and exact-identity resale research.

Retailer stock is a published declaration, not a delivery reservation. Actual completed-sale history, seller eligibility, shipping/tax and all-in costs must be supported before a purchase recommendation.
cost: No added API subscription. Your network and retailer access must work.
limitation: The read-only cloud collector imported 1,328 distinct USD-priced products in its first verified pass. Actual counts and availability change. Some pages exceed the bounded response limit and are skipped visibly. This does not establish profitable opportunities or historical sales.

title: eBay Browse API
status: Implemented · production access required; live connection unverified
purpose: Potential current listing discovery. Active listings and asking prices do not prove completed sales.
steps: Create/sign in to your eBay developer account and obtain an approved Production keyset. Sandbox keys do not supply live listings.
Open Application Keys. App ID / Client ID goes in the app-key field; Cert ID / Client Secret goes in the app-secret field. Your Dev ID is not the client secret.
Check current Browse production access, API terms, personal research use, retention rights and quota. Confirm this use has no additional API charge before enabling it.
Enter credentials privately below, confirm permitted free access, enable live listings and save. No terminal restart or Ctrl+C is required. Blank fields preserve saved credentials.
Enabling adds three starter searches for tools, label printers and single-board computers. Add or pause your own searches in Settings.
Open Settings to see the first successful request or a specific access/network error. Credential presence alone does not mean connected.
Searches collect up to 200 listings/page and persist offsets within the 10,000-result search window. API next links are never followed to arbitrary hosts.

For products with explicit GTIN, pack and condition, the collector can check production item details for exact current asking-price comparables. Missing identity fields remain exceptions; asking prices are not sold-history data.
cost: Only enable after confirming permitted access with no additional API charge. Current program conditions and quotas must be checked in your account.
limitation: Active fixed-price asking-price listings only. No completed-sales or automatic resale eligibility. OAuth documentation was read; the Browse adapter is tested with synthetic HTTP responses and still requires actual production validation.

title: Amazon seller data and FBA
purpose: Seller-authorized fees, catalog/eligibility evidence and your own transaction history where entitled.
steps: FBA means Fulfillment by Amazon: you send inventory to Amazon, which stores and ships it for fees.
Check seller-account approval, category/brand restrictions and acceptable purchase documentation first.
Use your current fee schedule or Seller Central estimate to create a dated channel scenario.
Include inbound/prep, storage, returns, removal and any incremental subscription cost. An API estimate is not a guaranteed fee.
A future API connection would require seller authorization. This version accepts no Amazon tokens and submits no listings.
cost: Seller plan and fulfillment costs are separate from the $0 data budget. Verify the current country-specific schedule.
limitation: No Amazon public-sale history or unrestricted access is assumed. The official Product Fees model was read; seller entitlements and current account-specific fees remain unknown.

title: Walmart Marketplace and WFS
purpose: Potential seller-authorized catalog, inventory and fee evidence.
steps: WFS means Walmart Fulfillment Services: Walmart stores and fulfills approved inventory for fees.
Check seller approval, product restrictions and sourcing-document requirements.
Enter reviewed item-specific fees, delivery, returns and payout timing in a separate Walmart selling scenario.
Do not buy an API plan or provide a seller secret here; an authorized connector has not been implemented.
cost: Verify current seller and item-specific fulfillment costs on the official portal.
limitation: Current documentation was not accessible in this session; endpoints, quotas and eligibility are unverified.

title: Other selling channels and your own data
purpose: Compare inexpensive marketplaces, local sales, specialist venues and direct buyers without assuming one marketplace wins.
steps: Add a channel scenario using its actual fee schedule, conservative selling price and fulfillment method.
Record identity and seller eligibility evidence, supported demand quantity and conservative cash-recovery days.
Import your own dated completed sales separately from views, mentions and asking prices.
Use Inventory for lot costs, sales, refunds and returns. Review the capital planner before committing money.
cost: A free listing can still have selling, payment, shipping or operational costs. Enter them explicitly.
limitation: Entered evidence is an operator claim, not independently verified by the application. No seller-account mutation exists.

title: Keepa and premium market history
purpose: Potential licensed historical pricing or demand proxies, if access and later budget justify it.
steps: No Keepa key is required for this version.
Do not subscribe to fill an empty dashboard.
Reassess pricing, licensing, retention and whether its metrics actually improve decisions only when a later budget exists.
cost: No free API or confirmed transaction history is assumed.
limitation: Not integrated and not necessary for local research; a price/rank proxy must not become a claimed sale.
